ei.title: Chapter 4-10 1번: The Flexible Boundaries of Social Bonds
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: Our complex brains might have evolved to establish strong social bonds, but defining what should be part of that social group appears to be rather flexible. For instance, some people treat their pets as if they are members of their family, and believe they can relate to the pets' needs, desires, fears and dreams. Others see animals as distinct from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to serve as some link to their existence. Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us still attribute certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.

② relate — 공감하다, 원문 일치
③ serve — 역할을 하다, 원문 일치
④ attribute — 부여하다, 원문 일치

det.korean: 사회 집단의 범위를 정의하는 것은 상당히 유연해(rather flexible) 보인다.

① completely controlled by logic — 논리에 의해 완전히 통제(본문에 논리 언급 없음)
② limited to close family members — 가까운 가족으로 제한(반려동물/무생물 예시와 모순)
③ impossible to change over time — 시간이 지나도 변경 불가(유연하다는 본문과 반대)
④ rather flexible — 상당히 유연한 ←정답

② 동물을 구별하는 사람도 있음(Others) → '모든 사람 공통'은 틀림
③ 유골이 존재와의 연결고리라고 믿는다 — 원문 일치 ←정답
④ many of us still attribute ~ → 부여한다고 명시 → '부여할 수 없다'는 반대
det.tip: believing those ashes serve as some link = 유골이 연결고리 역할을 한다고 믿으며
